Profiling on a Pixel 6a (dev build) traced this to components on the home screen with https:// sources — both expo-image and RN Image keep the View hierarchy invalidating continuously when fed remote URIs. The threshold showed up between 8 and 11 mounted remote-icon Image instances; below that, idle CPU was at the app baseline (~18%). Two contributors: AppIcon used expo-image with remote URLs for store-installed apps. AllAppsGridSheet kept its mounted while the bottom sheet was closed, so 80+ remote-icon Images were rendering off-screen. Fix: New useCachedRemoteImageSource hook: for https:// sources, asks expo-image for the disk-cache path (prefetching if needed), returns {uri: "file://..."}. candidates.title: Document and enhance HeyCyan Bluetooth-first WiFi transfer sequence
candidates.summary: Document and enhance HeyCyan Bluetooth-first WiFi transfer sequence This commit permanently documents the complete HeyCyan WiFi transfer sequence in the codebase with comprehensive comments and adds critical device status verification to prevent connection failures. ## Enhanced WiFi Transfer Sequence: 1. Bluetooth Connection: Connect to glasses device 2. Request WiFi Transfer: openWifiWithMode:QCOperatorDeviceModeTransfer 3. Receive Credentials: Get SSID and password from glasses 4. Wait for Hotspot Ready: getDeviceWifiIPSuccess with retry logic 5. Get Device IP: Receive IP address when hotspot is broadcasting 6. Configure iOS WiFi: Apply NEHotspotConfiguration with credentials 7. Check device status: getDeviceConfigWithFinished (NEW - CRITICAL VERIFICATION) 8. Wait for Connection: 5-second delay for iOS to establish connection 9. Test Connection: HTTP request to device IP 10. Start Transfer: Begin media download ## Key Improvements: - Added getDeviceConfigWithFinished status check aft
